text: I'll start by establishing the aerofoil section geometry (parametric, in mm) and checking it numerically before any 3D work.
Section checks out (t_max 6.01%, camber 4%). Now the 3D blade: sections wrapped onto cylinders, lofted, extended slightly past hub and shroud for clean cutting.
The `loft` wrapper expects faces; my sections are non-planar wires on cylinders, so I use `Solid.make_loft` directly. Re-emitting with the import inside.
Blade x-extent (−16.2) is far outside the expected ±9.7 — likely spline overshoot at the sharp trailing edge. Let me check a single section wire before trusting the loft.
Wires are exact; the loft bbox is probably OCC's inflated estimate. Let me tessellate the solid and measure real extents.
Smooth lofting across the twisted sections overshoots badly. Ruled loft with more radial stations keeps it on the sections.
Ruled loft on periodic splines fails; I'll rebuild each section as two splines (upper, lower) meeting at sharp LE/TE, with the trailing edge closed exactly.
Extents now match the sections exactly. Quick volume sanity check against the 2D section area.
Volume is 35% below the analytic estimate — I need to check the solid is actually valid and not self-tangled.
Blade solid is invalid. Switching to polyline sections for a robust ruled loft, and checking validity/volume immediately.
Volume still short of estimate — let me just look at the 2D loop and the wrapped section to see what shape I'm actually lofting.
Sections are right; volume debate aside, time to get something on disk. Building the sector and cutting both blades.
Fluid volume is valid and single-bodied; removed volume 891 mm³ matches the analytic blade volume between hub and tip (972·45/49 = 892). Now classify the faces.
